# Dedalo

> Dedalo compiles a text description of a tabletop-RPG dungeon into a map. One Rust core powers a command-line binary, a static web editor and an MCP server.

# Dedalo quickstart

Dedalo compiles a text description of a dungeon into a map. A file has the
extension `.dedalo` and holds one `dungeon` block.

```hcl
dungeon "crypt" {
    name = "The Crypt"

    room "entrance" {
        name = "Entrance"
        shape = rectangle(8, 6)

        feature "torch" {
            type = lighting
            subtype = torch
            placement { wall = south, offset = 2 }
        }
    }

    room "vault" {
        shape = square(6)
        layout { north_of = "entrance" }

        entity "skeletons" {
            type = creature
            position = [1, 1]
            properties { count = 3 }
        }
    }

    connection "vault_door" {
        from = "entrance"
        to = "vault"
        type = door
    }
}
```

## The working loop

1. Write or change the file.
2. `dedalo validate FILE` and apply the fixes it proposes. Every diagnostic
   names the element, the value found and the values allowed.
3. `dedalo inspect FILE --text-map` to read the result as text.
4. `dedalo render FILE` to write the map. `--preset player` hides everything
   the players must not see.

## Rules worth knowing

- Coordinates are cells. X grows east, Y grows south, north is up.
- Place rooms relative to each other (`north_of`, `south_of`, `east_of`,
  `west_of`, with `align` and `offset`) rather than by absolute position:
  no arithmetic, fewer mistakes. The first room is placed at `[0, 0]`.
- A `position` inside a room counts cells from 0 at the room's top-left
  corner. `placement { wall = north, offset = 2 }` and
  `placement { anchor = center }` avoid counting altogether.
- A connection joins two rooms that share a wall. Rooms that do not touch
  are joined by a `corridor "id" { connects = ["a", "b"] }`.
- IDs are lowercase with digits and underscores, and unique in the dungeon.
- Game data goes in `properties { }`. `dedalo catalog TYPE` lists the
  properties of a type; a name starting with `x_` is always accepted.
- Traps, creatures, items and notes are visible to the DM only by default.
  `visibility = dm` hides a whole room; `type = secret_door` hides a door.

## More

- `dedalo catalog` lists element types and subtypes.
- `dedalo explain CODE` describes a diagnostic code with a worked fix.
- `dedalo guide examples/forgotten_crypt` prints a complete example;
  `examples/levels_tower` shows a dungeon on several levels.
- `dedalo schema document` prints the JSON Schema of the document model;
  `dedalo convert FILE --to json` switches between the two spellings.

# Dedalo syntax

A file holds an optional `dedalo` header block and one `dungeon` block. The
syntax is a strict subset of HCL: blocks, attributes, literals, lists,
objects and shape calls. There are no expressions and no templates.

```hcl
dedalo {
    version = 1
}

dungeon "crypt" {
    name = "The Crypt"

    grid {
        unit = "5ft"
    }

    settings {
        default_wall = stone
        seed = 7
    }

    room "entrance" {
        name = "Entrance"
        shape = rectangle(8, 6)
        tags = ["entrance"]

        properties {
            description = <<-EOT
                Cold air rises from the stairs.
                EOT
        }
    }
}
```

## Values

| Type | Written as | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Number | Decimal, at most three decimals | `width = 2`, `offset = 1.5` |
| String | Double quotes, or a heredoc | `name = "Ingresso"` |
| Boolean | `true`, `false` | `locked = true` |
| Symbol | Bare word; dotted when from a plugin | `type = door`, `wall = north` |
| Reference | Quoted element ID | `from = "entrance"` |
| Point | Two numbers | `position = [3, 2]` |
| List | Brackets | `tags = ["combat"]` |
| Shape | A call | `shape = circle(3)` |

`null` unsets an optional attribute. Comments are `#`, `//` and `/* */`.
Escapes in strings: `\n`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\`, `\uXXXX`. The sequences `${` and
`%{` are not allowed. A one-line block holds one attribute:
`layout { north_of = "entrance" }`.

## Blocks

| Block | Label | Inside | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | ID | `dungeon` | One floor of a multi-level dungeon: a `name`, rooms and corridors |
| `room` | ID | `dungeon`, `level` | A space with a `shape` |
| `corridor` | ID | `dungeon`, `level` | Joins two spaces: `connects = ["a", "b"]` |
| `connection` | ID | `dungeon` | A door or passage: `from`, `to`, `type` |
| `feature` | ID | `dungeon`, `room`, `corridor` | Fixed element: furniture, trap, light, terrain |
| `entity` | ID | `dungeon`, `room`, `corridor` | Creature, NPC or item |
| `note` | ID | anywhere | Annotation: `text`, optional `target`, `position` |
| `layout` | none | `room` | Placement of the room |
| `placement` | none | `connection`, `feature`, `entity` | Wall or anchor placement |
| `properties` | none | any element | Typed game data from the catalog |
| `render`, `legend` | none | `dungeon`, `export` | Theme, labels and legend |
| `export` | optional name | `dungeon` | One output configuration |

## IDs

An ID is lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter,
at most 64 characters. All IDs share one namespace per dungeon: a room and a
feature cannot share an ID. References may point forward.

## Connections

`type` is one of `door`, `archway`, `open`, `stairs`, `ladder`, `trapdoor`.
`locked_door` and `secret_door` are accepted and mean `door` with
`properties { locked = true }` or `secret = true`. A secret door is hidden
from players. Stairs, ladders and trapdoors take a `position` inside `from`
and may omit `to`. With a `to`, `to_position` is the cell in that room where
they arrive, drawn as a second marker.

```hcl
connection "vault_door" {
    from = "entrance"
    to = "vault"
    type = door
    placement { wall = north, offset = 3, width = 2 }
}
```

## Levels

A dungeon on several floors groups its rooms and corridors in `level`
blocks. Each level is laid out on its own: placement, corridors and doors
stay inside one level, and only stairs, ladders and trapdoors join two. A
dungeon with levels keeps every room and corridor in one of them;
connections, notes and exports stay in the `dungeon` block.

```hcl
dungeon "tower" {
    level "ground" {
        name = "Ground floor"

        room "hall" {
            shape = rectangle(8, 6)
        }
    }

    level "upper" {
        name = "Upper floor"

        room "study" {
            shape = circle(3)
        }
    }

    connection "spiral" {
        from = "hall"
        to = "study"
        type = stairs
        position = [6, 1]
        to_position = [1, 3]
    }

    export "upstairs" {
        preset = player
        level = "upper"
    }
}
```

A map shows every level side by side, each under its name. An export with
`level`, or `dedalo render --level upper`, draws one. A level with nothing
an audience may see is left out of that audience's map, name included.

## Visibility

`visibility` is `public`, `dm`, `conditional` (with `reveal_when = "tag"`) or
`hidden`. Traps, creatures, items, chests and notes default to `dm`. A room
with `visibility = dm` disappears from player maps together with its doors.

## Exports

```hcl
export "players" {
    preset = player          # dm, player or clean
    format = png             # svg, png, pdf or txt
    cell_px = 70
    rotation = 90
    level = "upper"          # one level of a multi-level dungeon
    revealed = ["pit_found"]
    include = ["vault_door"] # shown although secret
    visibility { grid = false }
}
```

`dedalo render FILE --all` writes every export. A PDF export with
`scale = tabletop` prints one cell per inch, tiled across `page`-sized sheets.

## Language

The words a map prints by itself are English or Italian: the legend labels
of the built-in types, the headings `Legend` and `Notes`, and the scale
line. Names, notes and custom labels are yours and are never translated.

```hcl
dungeon "cantina" {
    render {
        language = it        # en (default) or it
    }

    room "cantina" {
        name = "Cantina"
        shape = rectangle(6, 4)
    }
}
```

`render` inside an `export` overrides it for that export, and
`dedalo render --lang it` for one command. A legend `entry` block still
replaces any single label.

## Templates

A template holds defaults for blocks that use it. Values the block sets win;
`properties` merge. Templates sit at the top of the file or in the dungeon,
and packs can provide them as `pluginid.name`.

```hcl
dungeon "barracks" {
    template "iron_door" {
        type = door

        placement {
            width = 2
        }

        properties {
            locked = true
        }
    }

    room "west" {
        shape = rectangle(6, 4)
    }

    room "east" {
        shape = rectangle(6, 4)
        layout { east_of = "west" }
    }

    connection "between" using "iron_door" {
        from = "west"
        to = "east"
    }
}
```

## Plugins

A plugin adds themes, element types, templates, painters, scene passes,
exporters, validators or shapes. Require it in the header and use its names
with its ID as prefix:

```hcl
dedalo {
    version = 1

    plugin "hand_drawn" {
        version = "^1.2"
    }
}

dungeon "sketch" {
    render {
        theme = hand_drawn.sepia
    }

    room "hall" {
        shape = rectangle(6, 4)
    }
}
```

`dedalo plugin add SOURCE` installs a plugin package and records it in
`dedalo.lock`. The source is a package folder, a zipped `.dedalopkg` file,
or the address of one; `--sha256 HASH` refuses a package with another hash.
`--plugin PATH` loads a folder or a `.dedalopkg` for a single command.

# Dedalo layout

Coordinates count cells. X grows east and Y grows south; north is the top of
the page. Rooms are polygons on the grid, walls are their edges, and doors
are openings cut where two rooms touch.

## Shapes

| Shape | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `square(side)` | Square |
| `rectangle(width, height)` | Rectangle |
| `circle(radius)` | Circle in a `2r` by `2r` box |
| `ellipse(width, height)` | Ellipse in a `width` by `height` box |
| `l_shape(width, height, cutout)` | Rectangle with its north-east corner cut away; `cutout` is a side or `[width, height]` |
| `polygon([[x, y], ...])` | Simple polygon, any winding, edges of any direction |

Doors go on any edge of a polygon, slanted ones included. Circles and
ellipses take doors at their four compass points, or anywhere with a
`bearing`. See Doors below.

`rotation = 90` turns a room clockwise in quarter turns; its contents and
wall names turn with it.

## Placing rooms

Prefer relative placement: no arithmetic.

```hcl
room "vault" {
    shape = square(6)
    layout {
        north_of = "entrance"   # also south_of, east_of, west_of
        align = start           # start, center (default) or end
        offset = 1              # shift along the shared side, in cells
        gap = 0                 # space between the two rooms
    }
}
```

- `align = start` lines up the west edges (north or south placement) or the
  north edges (east or west placement).
- `layout { position = [x, y] }` fixes the top-left corner on the map.
- The first room is placed at `[0, 0]` unless some room has a position.
- A room with no `layout` goes next to a placed room it has a connection or
  corridor with, on the side its door names, else the first free side.
- Rooms may touch but not overlap. An `OVERLAP` error proposes the smallest
  `offset` that clears it; `align` often fixes it too.

## Doors

A connection needs the two spaces to share a wall. `placement.wall` is the
side of `from`; `offset` counts cells from the west end of a north or south
wall, or the north end of an east or west wall. Without `offset` the door is
centred on the shared part. Walls up to `settings.max_stub` cells apart
(default 2) get a short stub passage automatically.

On a polygon, `wall` picks the edges that face that way, and
`placement { edge = 3 }` picks one edge by its index, counted from the first
vertex. A door on a slanted edge needs the other room to share that edge.
Its `offset` and `width` are measured along the edge, from its west end, or
from its north end when the edge is steeper than 45 degrees.

On a circle or an ellipse, `placement { bearing = 70 }` puts the door at the
point of the wall 70 degrees clockwise from north; 0 is north and 90 is
east. The bearing turns with the room when the room is rotated. The passage
runs straight out of the nearest compass side, so the other room must face
that part of the wall; when it does not, the error gives the bearings that
work.

```hcl
dungeon "rotunda" {
    room "hub" {
        shape = circle(4)
    }

    room "east" {
        shape = rectangle(3, 6)
        layout { east_of = "hub" }
    }

    connection "side_door" {
        from = "hub"
        to = "east"
        type = door
        placement { bearing = 70 }
    }
}
```

With levels, each level has its own plane: `position` and corridor `path`
points are counted on the level's own map, and the first room of each level
is placed at `[0, 0]`.

## Corridors

```hcl
corridor "hall" {
    connects = ["entrance", "vault"]
    width = 1
}
```

An automatic corridor runs straight between facing walls; when the rooms are
placed relative to each other the gap defaults to the corridor's `length`, or
2. An explicit `path` lists lattice points along the centre line, with
horizontal and vertical segments only; with an odd width use half cells
(`[4, 2.5]`). Both ends must touch the two spaces.

## Elements

```hcl
feature "table" {
    type = furniture
    subtype = table
    position = [3, 2]                     # top-left cell, from 0, in the room
}
feature "torch" {
    type = lighting
    subtype = torch
    placement { wall = south, offset = 2 } # against a wall
}
feature "altar" {
    type = furniture
    subtype = altar
    placement { anchor = center }          # also north, south_east, ...
}
```

In an 8 by 6 room, one-cell positions run from `[0, 0]` to `[7, 5]`. `size`
overrides the footprint; `rotation` turns it. Two blocking features may not
share a cell; creatures may stand on traps and rugs.

## Checking the result

`dedalo inspect FILE` prints each room's box on the map; `--text-map` draws
it: `#` wall, `.` floor, `+` door, `S` secret door, letters for elements.

# Dungeons in Markdown notes

A dungeon can live inside a Markdown note, such as a page of an Obsidian
vault, as a fenced code block whose language is `dedalo`. The Dedalo plugin
for Obsidian draws each block as a map where it stands. The `dedalo` command
and the MCP server read and write the block and leave the rest of the note
alone.

````markdown
## The forgotten crypt

The air smells of wet stone.

```dedalo player
dungeon "crypt" {
    name = "The Forgotten Crypt"

    room "entrance" {
        name  = "Entrance"
        shape = rectangle(8, 6)
    }
}
```

Read-aloud text and room descriptions go here, in Markdown.
````

## Fence options

Words after `dedalo` choose how the block is drawn. Flags on the command
line and tool arguments win over them.

| Option | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dm`, `player`, `clean` | | The audience; the same as `preset=...` |
| `preset` | `dm`, `player`, `clean` | The audience |
| `export` | an export name | Draw that `export` block of the dungeon |
| `level` | a level ID | Draw one level of a multi-level dungeon |
| `rotation` | `0`, `90`, `180`, `270` | Turn the map clockwise |
| `lang` | `en`, `it` | The language of default legend labels |
| `grid` | `true`, `false` | The grid |
| `labels` | `true`, `false` | Room labels |
| `notes` | `true`, `false` | The notes panel |

A value with spaces goes in double quotes: `level="ground floor"`.

## Several blocks in one note

Blocks are counted from 1 in reading order. Choose one with `--block N` on
the command line, or `block` in an MCP tool. `validate` and `fmt` take every
block when none is chosen; the other commands need a choice when the note
has more than one block. Diagnostics give the note's own line numbers.

A second block can show another part of the same adventure, but each block
is a whole dungeon: blocks do not share rooms. To show one dungeon to the DM
and to the players, use one block and switch the audience in Obsidian (each
map has a switch), or write two blocks with the same dungeon and different
options.

## Working in a note

1. Write the dungeon into the note. MCP: `dedalo_write` with the note's
   path replaces the note's only block, or the one given as `block`, and
   adds a block at the end when the note has none; `fence` sets the new
   block's options, such as `player`. By hand: write the fence and the
   dungeon with any editor.
2. `dedalo validate Note.md --json` (MCP: `dedalo_validate`) checks every
   block.
3. Fix: `dedalo validate Note.md --fix`, or edit by ID with
   `dedalo edit Note.md --block 2 --ops -` (MCP: `dedalo_edit` with `block`).
4. Look at it: `dedalo inspect Note.md --text-map`, or render a picture to
   check the layout: `dedalo render Note.md --format png -o map.png`.
5. `dedalo fmt Note.md` lays the blocks out canonically.

Keep the story in Markdown around the block, and inside the dungeon only
what belongs on the map: names, short `description`s, and `note` blocks for
numbered call-outs.

# Dedalo catalog

The class is the block keyword: `feature` or `entity`. Use `type = custom` for anything else, with `properties { symbol = "Al", label = "Altar of bones" }`.

| Type | Class | Category | Default visibility | Subtypes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `architecture` | feature | features | public | column, pillar |
| `container` | feature | treasure | dm | chest |
| `creature` | entity | creatures | dm | free |
| `custom` | either | features | public | free |
| `furniture` | feature | features | public | table, chair, wardrobe, altar, statue, sarcophagus, crate |
| `item` | entity | treasure | dm | treasure, key, weapon, armor, scroll, generic |
| `lighting` | feature | lighting | public | torch, brazier, candle, glowing_crystal |
| `mechanism` | feature | mechanisms | public | lever, button, generic |
| `npc` | entity | creatures | dm | free |
| `terrain` | feature | terrain | public | water, lava, rubble, rocks |
| `trap` | feature | traps | dm | pressure_plate, dart_launcher, pit, generic |

Read `catalog/<type>` for the properties of one type.

# Dedalo diagnostic codes

Read `errors/<CODE>` for causes and a worked fix.

- `SYNTAX_ERROR` (Error): The text is not valid Dedalo syntax.
- `UNKNOWN_BLOCK` (Error): A block keyword is not valid at this place.
- `UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE` (Error): An attribute name is not defined for this block.
- `TYPE_MISMATCH` (Error): A value has the wrong type.
- `INVALID_VALUE` (Error): A value has the right type but is not allowed.
- `UNKNOWN_PROPERTY` (Warning): A property is not defined by the catalog for this element type.
- `DUPLICATE_ID` (Error): Two elements share one ID.
- `UNKNOWN_REFERENCE` (Error): A reference names an element that does not exist.
- `UNKNOWN_TYPE` (Error): An element type or subtype is not in the catalog.
- `INVALID_SHAPE` (Error): A shape cannot be built.
- `LAYOUT_CYCLE` (Error): Rooms are placed relative to each other in a loop.
- `LAYOUT_UNDERCONSTRAINED` (Error): A room has no layout and nothing links it to a placed room.
- `OVERLAP` (Error): The interiors of two spaces intersect.
- `OUT_OF_BOUNDS` (Error): An element lies outside its room.
- `DOOR_NOT_PLACEABLE` (Error): A connection's opening does not fit on the wall the two spaces share.
- `UNRESOLVABLE_CONNECTION` (Error): The two spaces of a connection neither share a wall nor face each other closely.
- `CORRIDOR_DISCONNECTED` (Error): A corridor does not reach the spaces it connects.
- `ELEMENT_OVERLAP` (Warning): Two blocking features share a cell.
- `UNREACHABLE_ROOM` (Warning): A room cannot be reached from the entrance.
- `REFERENCED_ELEMENT` (Error): An element cannot be removed because others refer to it.
- `STALE_SOURCE` (Error): The file changed since the edit was prepared.
- `PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND` (Error): The document requires a plugin that is not installed.
- `PLUGIN_CONFLICT` (Error): Two active plugins claim the same exclusive role.
- `PLUGIN_FAILED` (Error): A plugin returned an error or invalid output.
- `PLUGIN_TIMEOUT` (Error): A plugin exceeded its time or memory budget.
- `PLUGIN_RULE` (Warning): A plugin validator reported a problem.
- `EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` (Error): The output image would exceed 16,384 pixels on one side.
